title: Stool test for hidden blood
what: This test looks for blood in your stool that you cannot see. It is a simple way to spot early signs of bowel polyps or tumors.
why: Usually for screening from about age 45 to 50, or with anemia or changes in bowel habits. The doctor decides.
duration: 5 minutes to collect at home; results in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: If your piles are bleeding right now
If you are on your period. It is better to do the test later

prepare.title: Container
prepare.text: Get the special container with a stick from the lab. The test cannot be done from a regular jar.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: The modern FIT test needs no diet. If your test is a different type, ask the lab.

steps: Collect your stool so it does not fall into the water, for example onto paper
Use the stick from the container to take a little stool from a few places
Put the stick back in the container and close it tightly
Take it to the lab within the time you are given
after: A positive test is not a diagnosis. The doctor usually refers you for a colonoscopy to find the cause
red_flags: Visible blood in your stool or black stools: do not wait for the result. See a doctor

faq.q: If the test is positive, is it cancer?
faq.a: Most often, no. Blood can come from piles, a small tear, or a polyp. But the cause must be found, usually with a colonoscopy.
